review_notes: I read the whole file and compared the repeated algHom_ext/ext/simp compatibility checks (`projection`, `compatibility`, `compatible`) and the augmentation-ideal membership transports (`mapsToKernel`, `map_augmentationIdeal`, the first half of `squareZeroQuotientEquiv_cotangentIdeal`). Those are short, or they differ in substance, so I did not report them. The one clear repeat is the argument that a ring map sending I into J sends I^2 into J^2. It appears in `descends` (inside `squareZeroQuotientEquiv`) and in `squareZeroQuotientMap`. I grepped Mathlib's Ideal directory for an existing lemma of this kind (names like pow_le_comap and map_pow_le) and found only `Ideal.map_pow`. The same file's other `pow_le_pow_left'` uses are for submodules and are not the same argument. I did not compile the proposed lemma, so its exact form is unchecked, and its instance requirements may need small adjustment.

findings.problem: The same ideal-power argument is written out twice. Given a ring map g with I ≤ comap g J and x ∈ I^2, you get g x ∈ J^2. Both proofs do the same four steps: push x into `Ideal.map g (I^2)` with `Ideal.mem_map_of_mem`, rewrite with `Ideal.map_pow`, turn the hypothesis into `map g I ≤ J` with `Ideal.map_le_iff_le_comap`, then apply `pow_le_pow_left'` at exponent 2. The first copy is in `descends` (lines 140–152, forward : Sym → TrivSqZeroExt, J = kerIdeal). The second is in the proof term of `squareZeroQuotientMap` (lines 351–362, g = map f, J = the target augmentation ideal). Each copy carries its own `mapped` and `inclusion` bookkeeping, so a change to the argument has to be made in both places.
findings.proposed_change: Add one private or public lemma before `squareZeroQuotientEquiv`: `theorem map_mem_pow_of_le_comap {A B : Type*} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] (g : A →+* B) {I : Ideal A} {J : Ideal B} (h : I ≤ J.comap g) (n : ℕ) {x : A} (hx : x ∈ I ^ n) : g x ∈ J ^ n`. Proof sketch: `have m := Ideal.mem_map_of_mem g hx; rw [Ideal.map_pow] at m; exact pow_le_pow_left' (Ideal.map_le_iff_le_comap.mpr h) n m`. Then `descends` becomes `simpa only [TrivSqZeroExt.kerIdeal_sq, Ideal.mem_bot] using map_mem_pow_of_le_comap forward.toRingHom mapsToKernel 2 hx`. This works because `mapsToKernel` already has the shape ∀ x ∈ I, forward x ∈ J, which is the unfolded `I ≤ J.comap forward`. The map definition becomes `Ideal.quotientMapₐ _ (map f) (fun x hx => map_mem_pow_of_le_comap (map f).toRingHom (map_augmentationIdeal f) 2 hx)`. Both uses are over CommRing, so the hypotheses hold.
findings.benefit: The two definitions shrink to their mathematical content: `forward` kills the square, and `map f` preserves the squares. The ideal-power manipulation is proved once and named, and any later square-zero construction in this file or in the library can reuse it.

evidence.excerpt: protected theorem map_pow (n : ℕ) : map f (I ^ n) = map f I ^ n
